formation_structure.execution_semantics: All actions are fixed. Conditions below are validity assertions, not executable branches, automatic waits or actions on dead units.
formation_structure.medical_geometry: Ansel [5,6] DOWN covers central rows 2–5 and columns 5–7, including Fang, Friston and initial Steward. His skill extends far enough to reach Midnight [1,5]. Spot's active nine-cell range includes Ansel diagonally, but excludes Friston and initial Steward. Melantha [4,4] receives no assumed ordinary healing.

mortal_gap_check.ansel_two_shell_bound: At full 1135 HP, two 891 hits require more than 647 healing between them. One boosted Ansel heal of 506.8 is insufficient; adding one delivered Spot heal of 464 gives a positive margin of 323.8 before other damage.
mortal_gap_check.first_skill_window: Spot deployed at 1968 first becomes ready after 450 inactive frames; activation 2419 is intended to add healing before a second medic splash near the historical 2443 window.
mortal_gap_check.late_pressure: Without Hibiscus, Friston cannot rely on the historical dual-medic mixed-wave budget. Melantha's lower-central damage must shorten overlaps sufficiently; she cannot heal or increase his block capacity.
mortal_gap_check.spot_shell_bound: A 1000-ATK physical shell deals 558 to catalog-DEF Spot. Three shells consume 1674 of 1833 HP before officer damage; healing timing remains necessary.
mortal_gap_check.unclosed_risk: Spot cannot repeat until 4370. The return through the lower artillery patrol before then must be survived by Ansel's actual healing allocation and HP reservoir. This is not proven by average HPS and is the leading counterexample to the selection.

formation_structure.opening: Retain the supported four-lane opening geometry because each unit has an independent interception duty. Replace the exposed lower attacker with Spot earlier than the historical post-lock withdrawal; eliminate Hibiscus's slot and reassign her healing obligations explicitly.

replacement.beneficiaries: Spot preserves the lower corridor; his active healing supports Ansel, allowing Steward's damage window.
replacement.changed_behavior: This plan withdraws before that historical cast, not after lock. Spot deliberately remains available to absorb a subsequent shell; no projectile cancellation or historical target assignment is assumed.
replacement.cooldown: Only an actual artillery cast consumes cooldown. Retreat itself neither consumes nor resets it.
replacement.known_reference: The saved eight-ID execution destroyed the lower eastern restraint at 1966 and later withdrew Melantha after projectile birth at 2054.
replacement.residual_risk: Born shells persist. New targeting can change when Melantha disappears. A live released enemy, uncleared restraint or premature civilian exposure invalidates the handoff.
replacement.survival_requirement: Melantha must be alive, her held enemies dead and the eastern lower restraint destroyed before withdrawal. Spot must establish blocking before any new lower officer passes.

tactical_thesis: Test a seven-ID staged replacement: Melantha establishes lower-outer interception and destroys its eastern restraint, then Spot replaces her before crossing artillery exposure. Spot combines blocking with healing Ansel; Ansel retains extended upper-lane healing. Returning Melantha accelerates lower-central clearance, while Steward rotates from artillery to armor. This removes Hibiscus but does not establish survival: consecutive lower-patrol shells and the later single-medic central workload remain decisive, model-checkable risks.
